posts.facebook:
Our Lady of the Rosary, this month is yours.

Teach us to pray it the way it actually gets prayed.

Four minutes in a parked car.
One decade before the kettle boils.
A bead held in the dark without a single word.

Count every one of them.

Keep the ones we love inside every mystery we manage.

Amen.

posts.facebook:
Jesus, mercy.
Father, hold us.

Not in a quiet room, not in front of a candle.
Here, at a red light.
In the ten steps between one room and the next.

Take the prayer that fits in the gaps,
because the gaps are most of the day.

Saint Benedict, guard this house
and everyone whose name I carry in it.

Amen.

posts.facebook:
Blessed Mother Mary, some of us have asked so long
that the words have gone quiet in the mouth.

So we come to you instead,
the way a family goes to the one who is closest to him.

Carry what we have been carrying.

Say our names to your Son
in the voice he has known the longest.

Amen.

posts.facebook:
Lord, bless this house and everyone who comes through its door.

The ones who live here.
The ones who visit.
The ones who left and might come back.

Give us one unhurried day.
Let rest be allowed, since rest was your own instruction.

Then go on ahead of us into the week we cannot see.

Amen.

posts.facebook:
Blessed Mother, today we pray the Joyful Mysteries with you.

An angel at the door.
A cousin's embrace.
A birth in a borrowed place.
A child held up in the temple.
And three days of not knowing where your Son was.

You kept that one among the joyful.
Teach us to keep ours there too.

Amen.

posts.facebook:
Who are you praying for this week? First names only.

Three words is plenty. No story needed.

A prayer to say with the names in front of you:

Lord, every name here belongs to someone
who has been carried a long time.

Hold the ones we cannot reach.
Be nearer to them than we can get.

Amen.

posts.facebook:
Lord, there is someone missing from this table.

Distance has done its slow work.
Three states, or three streets
and a conversation nobody wants to start.

Close it however you choose.
By a phone call, a holiday, a change of heart,
or by keeping us both here long enough to try again.

Saint Benedict, pray for the one who is far.

Amen.
